knowledge_point.title: Identifying Parallel Lines Given in Standard Form

question.:question/problem: Which of the following lines is parallel to $-3x + 4y = 12$?
question.:question/worked-solution:
For two lines to be parallel, they must have the same slope.

To find the slope of the line $-3x + 4y = 12$, we convert to slope-intercept form:

$$
\begin{aligned}
-3x + 4y &= 12 \\
4y &= 3x + 12 \\
y &= \frac{3}{4}x + 3
\end{aligned}
$$

In slope-intercept form, the slope is the $x$-coefficient. So, the slope is $\frac{3}{4}$.

From the given options, the only line that has a slope of $\frac{3}{4}$ is

$$
y = \frac{3}{4}x - 18
$$

question.:question/problem: Which of the following lines is parallel to $9x - 4y = 11$?
question.:question/worked-solution:
For two lines to be parallel, they must have the same slope.

To find the slope of the line $9x - 4y = 11$, we convert to slope-intercept form:

$$
\begin{aligned}
9x - 4y &= 11 \\
-4y &= -9x + 11 \\
y &= \frac{9}{4}x - \frac{11}{4}
\end{aligned}
$$

In slope-intercept form, the slope is the $x$-coefficient. So, the slope is $\frac{9}{4}$.

From the given options, the only line that has a slope of $\frac{9}{4}$ is

$$
y = \frac{9}{4}x
$$
